note: Superseded collection attempts on the way to the published run. Each is retained with its actual failure; full raw directories are not committed. None produced a grade.

attempts.reason: The disposable App aborted before collection (SIGABRT, Avalonia RenderTimer error -6661): the desktop display was unavailable. Nothing was measured; the cause is the environment, not the suite.

The static-image suite completed but the animation observer refused its first request (diagnosed from the retained evidence and the fix: no animation frame was recorded): its prior-challenge allowance covered the input phase only, while the static-image phase adds 31 more pairs. Fixed in b8625ed5 with a regression test.

The animation suite reached its first build stage and refused the raw replies: the App acknowledged a=T with its placement id (i=<id>,p=1;OK) as the lifecycle contract documents, while the expected reply shape omitted it. The reply-format expectation was corrected in c9875876; no pixel result or grade was involved.

A complete 18/18 run (effect supported, receipt schema 70) on the App built from 479a5465. Superseded, not failed: review of the playhead found five defects (finite-loop count, catch-up after a long gap, loading resume timing, trailing gapless frame, wake-up on retire), fixed in b4bcba0d, so the changed App was rebuilt and the whole collection repeated. The retained report and receipt are the earlier verdict; the full archive (sha256 below) is in the history of commit 2838dbd9.

The disposable App (rebuilt after the review fixes) aborted before collection (SIGABRT, Avalonia RenderTimer error -6661) while the desktop session was locked and the display unavailable. Nothing was measured; the cause is the environment. The collection was repeated after waking the display.

A second complete 18/18 run (effect supported, receipt schema 70) on the App built from b4bcba0d. Superseded, not failed: further review rounds changed production code and the measuring scripts again (settling the playhead before gap or frame changes, arrival-anchored loading resume, wake-ups for an animation that cannot move, tolerated boundary-straddling capture pairs, eviction ordering, undecoded fallback for a rejected frame handle, bleed checks on both pair members, refusal in persistent sessions and parked-time rebasing), so the App and scripts were rebuilt and the whole collection repeated. The retained report and receipt are that run's verdict.
